problems: The page title says "Pipeline validation," but the only explanatory text describes a document-preview limit, not what validation checks or does
The page title doesn't match its navigation label, which is "Designer"
The "Enable pipeline validation" toggle has no supporting copy explaining its own purpose
No visual relationship (grouping, indentation, conditional state) shows whether the document limit depends on the toggle or is unrelated to it
Save is disabled by default with no explanation of why

annotations.callout: Users click Designer and a page with a different title opens.
Nothing on the page says what this toggle does.
Nothing shows that the relationship between the toggle and Maximum preview documents isn't clear — the document limit doesn't apply if validation is disabled.
Save is disabled and nothing says why.

annotations.callout: Credentials are never sent — where?

annotations.target: Use preview data for contextual metadata toggle
annotations.callout: Four toggles say “When disabled,” this one says “When enabled.”
No helper text explains what this setting controls, and it's not grouped with the toggles above.

issues.title: API Management page title doesn't cover both settings groups, and section scope is unclear

issues.summary: The page title doesn't cover the Developer Portal settings that live on the same page, and it's unclear which controls the Save button and which the Build site button actually apply to.

annotations.callout: The page title says API Management 3.0, but the page really configures the APIM 3.0 Developer Portal.
The toggle label packs three ideas into one run-on sentence.

No heading marks what Save applies to (fix: label it “Service publishing”), while the section below has its own separate Build site button that saves and rebuilds the portal at once, with no confirmation of that beyond its own progress label.
The example URL updates as users type, but that's a subtle hint easy to miss — nothing actually explains what's happening.
No explanation of where the logo appears or what constraints apply.

annotations.target: Allow Access to APIM 3.0 Portal pages without login toggle
annotations.callout: Uses title case, inconsistent with sentence-case labels everywhere else on the page.

issues.title: AutoSync page intro doesn't match its General tab, and a lone toggle requires an unnecessary Save
issues.screen: Admin Manager > Application Settings > AutoSync
issues.summary: The page intro only describes the Versions tab, a single toggle requires an unnecessary Save step, and nothing explains how the environment default Snap Pack version relates to each pipeline's own version.

annotations.callout: The intro describes upgrading pipelines — the Versions tab's job — but General loads first and has nothing to do with upgrading.

annotations.target: Allow nullable for last modified date toggle
annotations.callout: The description restates the same idea in three different sentences without adding new information.
A standalone toggle doesn't need a separate Save step.
The selector shows a raw build string with no explanation of what it controls.
Uses title case, inconsistent with sentence-case labels everywhere else on the page.
Uses a completely different version format than the selector above, with nothing tying the two together or explaining what Upgrade now does.

issues.title: Asset catalog access page doesn't explain the feature or its access options
issues.screen: Admin Manager > Application Settings > Asset catalog
issues.summary: The intro just restates the page title instead of explaining what the Asset catalog is, and neither access option says what it actually grants.

annotations.callout: The intro just restates the page title — it doesn't say what the Asset catalog is or why access to it matters.
Nothing tells users what Everyone actually grants — can non-admins edit assets, or only view them?
This page auto-saves on selection with no confirmation, unlike other Admin Manager pages that use an explicit Save button — users may wonder if their change took effect.

issues.title: SSO configuration page confusing and sections in wrong order
issues.screen: Admin Manager > Security > Authentication > SSO tab
issues.summary: The page shows the paste-back step before the copy-out step, so users hit a dead end before they have anything to enter — with no indication they need to leave and return.

labels: Single Log Off Call Back URL
Add SnapLogic application in your identity provider
Provide SnapLogic metadata to your IdP
problems: Metadata upload section (second-visit task) appears at the top, before the SnapLogic-generated URLs the user needs first
No indication that this is a two-pass workflow requiring the user to leave and return
The page acts as both source (copy values out) and destination (paste metadata back) with no explanation of either role
Users attempt to upload IdP metadata before the IdP app exists, because they cannot yet have the metadata

proposed_fix.approach: Numbered two-step layout that makes the two-pass workflow explicit

steps.heading: Copy SnapLogic values for your identity provider
steps.body: Copy the values below and use them to create a SAML application in your identity provider (Okta, Azure AD, etc.). Then return to this page to complete Step 2.
elements: Download metadata file (alternative for IdPs that accept file format)

steps.heading: Upload your identity provider metadata
steps.subheading: Complete after finishing Step 1 in your identity provider
steps.body: After creating your SAML application in your IdP, export the metadata file and upload it here.

issues.interactive_description: Mini mock showing the two-pass flow: Step 1 (copy values) → tooltip or modal saying 'Now go configure your IdP and return' → Step 2 (upload metadata) becomes active

annotations.callout: Nothing above the tabs explains that one is for login and one is for API authentication.
Users see this first — but they can't complete it yet. The IdP app doesn't exist until they use values from lower on this same page.

annotations.target: Entity ID / Reply URL / Logout URL section
annotations.callout: The values users need first are presented second, with no instruction to copy them and go elsewhere.
This page plays two roles at two different times — source and destination — but nothing on the page communicates that.

issues.title: JWT authentication page doesn't explain the Disable basic authentication option or field limits
issues.screen: Admin Manager > Security > Authentication > JWT tab
issues.summary: The intro never mentions that Disable basic authentication enforces JWT-only auth, both URL fields truncate with no way to see the full value, and neither field says whether it's required.

annotations.callout: The intro explains JWT auth is optional but never mentions that the Disable basic authentication checkbox further down enforces JWT-only auth for the org.
Long URLs truncate with no tooltip, wrap, or way to view the full value users entered.
Neither field indicates whether it's required.
Save is disabled by default with no explanation of why.

issues.title: Users table doesn't clarify type icons, group membership, or who a role-change confirmation applies to
issues.screen: Admin Manager > User Management > Users
issues.summary: Type icons have no label, the role-change confirmation dialog doesn't name the user, the Groups count isn't clickable, and bulk actions (including Delete) are invisible until a row is selected.

annotations.callout: The Type column shows a user or service-account icon with no text and no tooltip, even though the Type filter menu already uses text labels for the same values.
Changing a role to Env admin opens a dialog that says "this user" instead of naming them, giving no way to catch a wrong-row click before confirming.
The Groups column shows only a number (or "-"). It isn't clickable and has no tooltip, so users can't tell which groups someone belongs to without leaving the page.

Delete only appears in each row's kebab menu, or after selecting one or more rows, which swaps the toolbar to reveal Access, Update auth, and Delete — with no hint beforehand that those actions exist.

issues.title: New user account-type page doesn't explain what really differs between types
issues.screen: Admin Manager > User Management > Users > New user
issues.summary: User and Team accounts look identical apart from one vague line, and Service account—the one type with a real capability restriction—has the least explanation of the three.

annotations.callout: Both show identical App access and API access checkmarks and near-identical description text; the only difference ("shared and managed by multiple people") doesn't explain what that means day to day.
Service account is the only type with an actual capability cut (no App access), but it's the card with the least explanation of the three.

issues.title: New user account dialog doesn't explain its Access sentence or what each checkbox grants
issues.screen: Admin Manager > User Management > Users > New user > User account
issues.summary: The Access sentence has a dangling conditional that misreads as applying to the whole list, none of the Access checkboxes explain what they grant, and the dialog has no Learn more link or tooltips anywhere.

annotations.callout: Unlike the account-type page, nothing here offers more explanation for Role, Access, or Authentication methods.

"Users with app access also have access to APIs, Monitor and Admin Manager (if they are an Environment admin)" reads as if Admin Manager access is an add-on, but Role is either User or Environment admin, not both. "App access" itself is never defined — it really means Designer access, and AutoSync isn't available without it.
Designer, AutoSync, and API access only have no helper text — an admin has to already know what each one grants before they can choose correctly.

issues.title: New team account dialog breaks the Role pattern, never explains what a maintainer does, and leaves Access unexplained
issues.screen: Admin Manager > User Management > Users > New user > Team account
issues.summary: Role breaks the radio-control pattern used elsewhere, the Maintainers field never says what a maintainer does, the Access sentence has a dangling conditional and never explains that "app access" means Designer access, and the dialog has no Learn more link or tooltips anywhere.

annotations.callout: Unlike the account-type page, nothing here offers more explanation for Maintainers, Role, Access, or Authentication methods.
The field just says "Maintainers" with a search box — nothing explains what selecting someone here actually does for them or the account.
The User and Service account dialogs both show Role as a radio control. Here it's plain text instead, so the same concept looks like two different features depending on which dialog you're in.

"Users with app access also have access to APIs, Monitor and Admin Manager (if they are an Environment admin)" references Environment admin, but team accounts are always locked to the User role — that clause can never apply here and only adds confusion. "App access" itself is never defined — it really means Designer access, and AutoSync isn't available without it.

issues.title: New service account dialog drops Access and Authentication with no explanation, and gives no Role guidance
issues.screen: Admin Manager > User Management > Users > New user > Service account
issues.summary: Role offers no guidance for a non-interactive account, the Access and Authentication sections present in the other dialogs disappear here with no explanation, and there is no Learn more link or tooltips anywhere.

annotations.callout: This account can't sign in through the UI, but nothing on the dialog says so — and unlike the User and Team dialogs, it has no Access or Authentication methods sections, with no explanation why. There's also no Learn more link for more detail.
The default role is User, yet many APIs require Environment admin permission — nothing on this dialog tells admins that before they create the account.

issues.title: Groups table has no sort, no bulk delete, and hides that rows are clickable
issues.screen: Admin Manager > User Management > Groups
issues.summary: The Groups table offers no sorting or pagination despite 1527 rows, leaves the Description column empty instead of showing useful dates, and gives rows no visual cue that clicking them opens the group.

annotations.callout: Only a name search box exists for 1527 groups — no column sorting and no pagination, just a scrollbar.
The Description column is empty for every row shown, and the table lacks columns like Date added and Updated date that the Users table already has.

Clicking anywhere on the row opens it for editing, but the group name isn't styled as a link, so nothing signals it's clickable. There's also no way to select multiple groups for deletion, unlike the Users table's row checkboxes and bulk delete.

issues.title: New group dialog warns the name can't be changed before the group even exists
issues.screen: Admin Manager > User Management > Groups > New group
issues.summary: "The group name cannot be changed" appears under an empty, active Group name field on the creation dialog, reading like a warning about a restriction that's already in effect before anything has been created.

annotations.callout: This line sits under an empty, active Group name field on the creation dialog — it reads like a warning about a restriction that's already in effect, when nothing has been created yet.

issues.title: Editing a group's members takes two saves, and Add users looks like a duplicate of member search
issues.screen: Admin Manager > User Management > Groups > Edit group
issues.summary: The Edit group heading gives no indication this is an edit dialog, adding a user to a group requires a save inside the Add users modal and a second save on the Edit group dialog (or the change is silently lost), and the modal itself looks and behaves differently from the account-creation dialogs elsewhere in Admin Manager.

annotations.callout: The page heading just shows the group's name — nothing indicates this is an edit dialog, so it can appear to an admin as a read-only detail view.

The "Search users by email or name" box and "+ Add users" link sit side by side but do unrelated things — search only filters existing members, while "+ Add users" is the only way to add someone new. The modal it opens also looks and behaves differently from the account-creation dialogs, and its trigger is a plain text link rather than a button.
Adding a user requires clicking Save inside the Add users modal, then clicking Save again in this dialog — skip the second Save and the added user is lost, with no warning that this is required.

issues.title: Role rows don't look clickable, and there's no way to see how to change who has a role
issues.screen: Admin Manager > User Management > Roles
issues.summary: Role names in the table look like plain text with no cue that clicking one opens its member list, and the read-only member list gives no indication that role membership is changed on the user's profile, not from here.

annotations.callout: Role names in the table look like plain text, and the intro ("View roles and their members") doesn't say clicking one opens its member list — admins have to discover it by trial and error.
This list is read-only — there's no add or remove control, and nothing tells the admin that role membership is set per-user rather than from here, so the page looks like a dead end.

issues.title: Pending Portal user requests are buried in the Users table and hard to act on
issues.screen: Admin Manager > User Management > Users
issues.summary: Portal user signups are mixed into the main Users table with no default indicator, the bare label "Portal" never says it means the APIM 3.0 Developer Portal, and even after finding a request, approving or rejecting it requires selecting the row or digging into its ⋮ menu.

annotations.callout: Portal users are mixed into the same Users table as everyone else, with no default indicator. A pending request only shows as the word "Pending" in the Access column — admins have to already know to set the Type filter to "Portal user" to find it.
Even after filtering to Portal users, Approve and Reject aren't visible on the row. Admins have to select the row's checkbox to reveal the actions in the toolbar, or open that row's ⋮ menu instead.

The Type filter and every reference to this account type use the bare word "Portal," with nothing to clarify it means the APIM 3.0 Developer Portal specifically — admins unfamiliar with that product area have no way to know what kind of account this is.

issues.title: Environment page gives no summary, and two fields go nowhere in the product
issues.screen: Admin Manager > System Configuration > Environment
issues.summary: The Environment page shows four tabs with no summary explaining what an environment is, a misleading "Read-only" note, an Environment ID with no context or copy button, and both the Environment description and Tag fields are dead ends — neither is ever displayed anywhere in the product.

annotations.callout: The page shows "Environment" and four tabs with no summary explaining what the tabs are for — admins have to click into each tab just to find out what it does.

The note under the tabs says "Read-only attributes for identification include a unique ID, name, and type" — but it never mentions the Environment description field, which admins can actually edit. Leading with "read-only" makes the entire tab sound uneditable.
The Environment ID is just a long string with no explanation of why it matters, and no copy affordance — admins have to select and copy the text by hand.

Admins can type a description and save it, but nothing in the product ever displays it — not this page, not the environment selector, nowhere. A field that quietly goes nowhere is very confusing for users, who have no way to know it's a dead end.

Same issue as the description field: admins can name a custom tag and save it, but that name is never displayed anywhere — including the environment selector, which only ever reads the icon and color, never the tag name.
Nothing on this tab says what the icon and color are for or where admins will see them — they have to pick something and guess.

issues.title: Snaplexes page and Add Snaplex dialog, multiple issues
issues.screen: Admin Manager > System Configuration > Snaplexes
issues.summary: Mislabeled controls, an undocumented internal value shown as a Snaplex type, and several Add/Update Snaplex dialog fields — Select project, Load balancer, Ultra load balancer — with real access or reliability consequences that go unexplained, compounded by field tooltips that are hidden behind hover on every tab.

annotations.callout: This control only ever creates a Groundplex — Cloudplex and AutoSync Snaplexes aren't customer-creatable, so "Add Snaplex" names the wrong thing. Admins have to contact their CSM to add a Cloudplex, and the current control gives no hint of that.
The toggle sits in a plain toolbar row below the fold of the page header, with no visual weight — easy to miss even though it applies to the entire environment.

The Type column shows "sidekick" for on-premises Snaplexes — a raw internal value that never appears anywhere in SnapLogic's own documentation. The docs describe exactly three types: Cloudplex, Groundplex, and AutoSync Snaplex. Admins have no way to know "sidekick" means Groundplex.

This value is an arbitrary node-binding identifier — combined with Location, it forms the Snaplex's runtime path and must match the JCC's local config — not the SnapLogic Environment shown elsewhere in Admin Manager. Renaming it after nodes are running breaks their binding.
The Location dropdown in the Add Snaplex dialog also defaults to "sidekick" — the same undocumented value, now in a dialog too.

annotations.target: Add Snaplex dialog Select project field
annotations.callout: If the admin selects a Project instead of shared, only users with permissions for that Project can use the Groundplex — the dropdown gives no indication of this.

Every field tooltip in this dialog is hidden by default — no icon, no visual cue that one exists. Admins have to hover over a field label and wait for it to appear. This applies across all four tabs: Settings, Logging, Node properties, and Node proxies.
Same hidden-tooltip issue as the Settings tab — this tab's field tooltips are hidden by default with no visible cue that one exists.

annotations.target: Add Snaplex dialog, Node properties tab
annotations.callout: Same hidden-tooltip issue as the Settings tab — this tab's field tooltips are hidden by default with no visible cue that one exists.

annotations.target: Add Snaplex dialog, Node proxies tab
annotations.callout: Same hidden-tooltip issue as the Settings tab — this tab's field tooltips are hidden by default with no visible cue that one exists.

annotations.target: Add Snaplex dialog Load balancer field
annotations.callout: If left blank, Triggered Tasks run through the Control Plane's cloud URL instead of the Snaplex — the path SnapLogic's own APIM best-practices doc warns against, requiring the Snaplex or an Alternative URL instead. Nothing on this field discloses that.

annotations.target: Add Snaplex dialog Ultra load balancer field
annotations.callout: If left blank, no run URL is ever set for Ultra Tasks — unlike the plain Load balancer field, there's no fallback. Ultra Tasks will fail to execute, with no warning on the field that this is a requirement.

issues.title: Cloudplex secure connectivity has no default filter, so deleted connections bury active ones
issues.screen: Admin Manager > System Configuration > Snaplexes > Cloudplex secure connectivity
issues.summary: The Cloudplex secure connectivity tab loads with no Status filter applied, so 29 of 30 permanently-listed Deleted connections bury the one Active connection.

annotations.callout: The tab loads with no Status filter applied — 29 of 30 rows here are Deleted. Deleted connections stay listed forever, so admins must manually filter every time just to see what's active.

issues.title: Git Integration gives no setup guidance, and known-fixed fields aren't pre-filled or explained
issues.screen: Admin Manager > System Configuration > Git Integration
issues.summary: Every provider other than GitHub.com and GitHub Enterprise Cloud requires registering SnapLogic as an app externally, then pasting values back into this page — but nothing on the page says so. Azure leaves its fixed, non-customer-specific Base URL and Authorized Scopes blank instead of pre-filling them the way GitLab cloud already does, and the GitLab Namespaces field accepts a real wildcard syntax with zero in-product explanation. Customers have consistently had trouble configuring these integrations.

annotations.callout: Every provider other than GitHub.com and GitHub Enterprise Cloud requires registering SnapLogic first, but nothing on the page says so — admins hit a blank form with no idea where these values come from.
Every other field says "URL" in caps — this one reads "Base url."

annotations.target: Azure Base URL and Authorized scopes fields
annotations.callout: Both fields are the same for every Azure customer per SnapLogic's docs, yet they're empty — Authorized scopes means typing an exact GUID string by hand. GitLab's equivalent fixed fields come pre-filled.
The field filters repos using comma-separated paths where * and ** mean different things — none of that is hinted at in the product.

issues.title: Custom privacy notice gives no URL format guidance, and the liability disclaimer is easy to skip
issues.screen: Admin Manager > System Configuration > Custom privacy notice
issues.summary: The Privacy notice page URL field gives no indication of the format it expects, even though SnapLogic's own docs confirm the real product validates it (must start with http, https, or www). The liability disclaimer below it is a real legal commitment but is styled as small italic grey fine print, easy to skip past.

annotations.callout: The field accepts a URL but gives no indication of the format it expects. SnapLogic's own docs confirm the real product validates this — a valid URL must start with http, https, or www — and shows explicit success or error messages after Save. None of that is hinted at here; admins only learn the rule by getting it wrong first.

The disclaimer confirms the admin is an authorized representative of their org and that the org "assumes full responsibility" and "will bear all liabilities" for the submitted URL — a real legal commitment. But it's styled as small italic grey text, the same visual weight as a caption.

issues.title: Snap Packs page doesn't explain that a version override replaces the environment default
issues.screen: Admin Manager > Subscriptions > Snap Packs
issues.summary: Overriding a Snap Pack's version in the table replaces the environment-wide default for that Snap Pack, but nothing on the page says so — and SnapLogic's own docs' warning to consult Support before overriding isn't reflected in the product either.

annotations.callout: An override to a Snap Pack's version in the table overrides the environment default for that Snap Pack, but nothing on the page says so.

issues.title: Left nav mislabels Password expiration, and the page doesn't explain what 0 means or how Expire all passwords really behaves
issues.screen: Admin Manager > Security > Password expiration
issues.summary: The left nav item reads "Password expiry" — British English, and a mismatch with the page's own "Password expiration" title. Expiration period defaults to 0 with no indication that means passwords never expire, and Expire all passwords silently skips SSO users and out-of-scope environments while burying the manual, per-account reset work it creates for service accounts.

annotations.callout: The left nav item reads "Password expiry" — British English — but the page it opens is titled "Password expiration," the American English term used everywhere else in the product.
Expiration period defaults to 0 with no explanation — admins can't tell whether that means passwords never expire or expire immediately.
Nothing on the page explains what Expiration notice period controls or how the notification actually reaches users — admins have to guess whether it's an email, an in-app banner, or something else.

Expire all passwords also expires every service account's credentials, but since they can't log in, their creating admin has to manually reset each one and update the dependent app — none of that is disclosed before confirming.

Expire all passwords sounds like it resets everyone's password, but it silently skips SSO users entirely, and also skips users whose accounts span environments you don't administer — none of this is disclosed on the page.

issues.title: Session timeout and Idle timeout look identical, but behave completely differently — and nothing on the page explains it
issues.screen: Admin Manager > Security > Session timeout
issues.summary: Session timeout and Idle timeout share the same range and default with no explanation that one is a silent absolute cutoff and the other warns before logging out, and setting Idle timeout higher than Session timeout silently makes it meaningless.

annotations.callout: Both sliders share the same 5–60 range and default to 60 minutes, with no hint that they work completely differently. Session timeout is a fixed, absolute cutoff from login — enforced by a cookie that expires regardless of activity — while Idle timeout only counts real inactivity, tracked across tabs.

Idle timeout shows a 2-minute warning before logging a user out, with a Continue option — but Session timeout gives no warning at all, so unsaved work in an active session can vanish the instant the fixed cutoff hits. Neither behavior is disclosed on the page.

If Idle timeout is set higher than Session timeout, the session's fixed cutoff always happens first, so the idle timer can never fire. Neither the page nor the backend validates or warns about this — unlike Password expiration's enforced notice/expire relationship.

issues.title: Email encryption skips a real setup step, its toggle only explains disabling, and the feature is invisible when not subscribed
issues.screen: Admin Manager > Security > Email encryption
issues.summary: The intro omits a real prerequisite (setting up encryption with the email provider) and gives no link to Global user settings, the toggle's helper text only explains disabling, and the page disappears entirely for environments not subscribed to Enhanced Email Encryption instead of surfacing an upsell opportunity.

annotations.callout: SnapLogic's docs confirm Admin Manager only includes this page in environments subscribed to Enhanced Email Encryption — but that means the feature is invisible rather than discoverable. An admin in an unsubscribed environment has no way to learn this capability exists.

The intro tells users to upload a public key in their Global user settings, but skips a real prerequisite confirmed in SnapLogic's docs: users must first set up encryption with their own email provider. There's also no link to Global user settings — just a description of where to go.

The toggle is labeled "Enable email encryption," but turning it on doesn't encrypt anything itself — it only lets users opt in by uploading their own key. The helper text only explains the disable behavior ("stops the encryption... to all users"), with nothing describing what enabling actually does.

issues.title: Allowlists: stale "contact Support" copy, an unexplained checkbox, overstated permanence, and an undisclosed node shutdown risk
issues.screen: Admin Manager > Security > Allowlists
issues.summary: The Cloud-triggered allowlist's Groundplex checkbox and the shared "permanently stored" helper text are both unexplained or inaccurate, the CORS allowlist's intro tells admins to contact Support for a feature that's fully self-service, and removing a Groundplex IP range can shut down a live node with no warning beyond a generic access-refused message.

annotations.target: Apply IP Allowlist to Groundplex Trigger and Ultra Tasks checkbox
annotations.callout: This checkbox has a real effect — checking it applies this same IP range to Groundplex Trigger and Ultra Tasks too, a different task type — but nothing on the page explains that, and the Learn more text only describes Cloud URL invocation, never mentioning the checkbox at all.

The helper text says IP ranges are "permanently stored," but the page has its own Remove control for these ranges — they aren't permanent at all. This could make admins hesitate to add a range they're actually free to undo later.

The intro text says domains must be added "through SnapLogic Support," but the UI below it is fully self-service — filling in a domain and clicking Add domain, then Save, works immediately with no Support ticket required. The same stale claim is repeated in SnapLogic's external docs.

The field accepts any text and saves it, but the stored value is used as a Python regex matched against the browser's Origin header (scheme://host[:port]) — with no format hint, an admin typing example.com instead of https://example\.com saves successfully but the entry never matches anything. Invalid or malformed entries fail silently, with no error shown.

Removing an IP range can shut down a live Groundplex node after a one-day grace period, but the modal that warns about it — which only appears when an existing node falls outside the new range — just says affected nodes will be "refused access" and pipelines "disconnected." It never mentions the 24-hour grace period, or that clicking Disconnect is what actually starts that countdown.
